skills.description: Make testable predictions and define observations that would reject the proposed mechanism.

skills.title: Controls & confounds
skills.description: Separate independent variables, controls, nuisance variables, and hidden joint interventions.

skills.title: Reproducibility
skills.description: Preserve commands, provenance, environments, metrics, failure rules, and immutable artifacts.

skills.title: BPE & BPB
skills.description: Reason from bytes through BPE to token loss and compare tokenizers with valid normalization.

skills.title: Tensor & compute accounting
skills.description: Trace shapes and calculate parameters, tokens, and approximate FLOPs.

skills.title: Learning dynamics
skills.description: Diagnose warmup, schedules, curve gaps, throughput drift, underfitting, and overfitting.

skills.title: Optimization interventions
skills.description: Interpret learning rate, batch, schedule, decay, clipping, and optimizer comparisons.

skills.title: Compute-matched comparison
skills.description: Distinguish fixed steps, tokens, FLOPs, parameters, and wall time.

skills.title: Implementation contracts
skills.description: Add controlled switches with tests, metadata, accounting, and baseline compatibility.

skills.title: Causal experimental inference
skills.description: Use effect sizes, confirmation, negative results, uncertainty, and decisive follow-ups.

skills.title: SFT objective & data
skills.description: Understand serialization, response-only masks, packing, optimizer state, and data mixtures.

skills.title: Capability & forgetting
skills.description: Measure instruction gains and retained base capability with frozen evaluations.

skills.title: DPO derivation
skills.description: Derive response log-ratio learning against a frozen reference and explain beta and length bias.

skills.title: DPO verification
skills.description: Hand-check the loss, test gradient behavior, audit preferences, and measure drift.

skills.title: Policy-gradient objective
skills.description: Trace on-policy rollouts, group baselines, masked log probabilities, and update behavior.

skills.title: RL evaluation & reward hacking
skills.description: Jointly analyze reward, pass@k, length, variance, cost, and verifier exploits.

skills.title: Frozen capstone protocol
skills.description: Run a fair compute-constrained search with sealed evaluation and exact reproduction.

skills.title: Calibrated scientific claims
skills.description: Connect claims to evidence, uncertainty, limitations, and negative results.

activities.title: Defend a controlled experiment
activities.summary: Establish the language and logic used by every later experiment.
activities.deliverable: Write roughly 300–600 words using the five numbered headings below. You do not need to run code or attach a file for this first challenge.
activities.prompt:
Write a response with five numbered sections:

1. Variables — For a learning-rate ablation, what is the independent variable and what is the dependent variable?
2. Fair comparison — What would you hold fixed? Name at least four controls.
3. Threats — Name one nuisance variable and one confound, and explain the difference.
4. Evidence — What can a smoke run prove, and what can it not prove? Give one quantitative result that would falsify your learning-rate hypothesis.
5. Budget — Give one sentence each for when you would compare fixed steps, fixed tokens, fixed FLOPs, and fixed wall time.
activities.answer_template:
1. Variables
Independent variable: …
Dependent variable: …

2. Fair comparison
I would hold fixed: …

3. Threats
Nuisance variable: …
Confound: …
The difference is: …

4. Evidence
A smoke run can prove: …
It cannot prove: …
My hypothesis is: …
I would reject it if, after [budget], [measurable result]: …

5. Budget
Fixed steps: …
Fixed tokens: …
Fixed FLOPs: …
Fixed wall time: …

lesson.title: Variables and fairness
lesson.body: The independent variable is the one intentional change. The dependent variable is the measured outcome. Controls are the conditions you deliberately keep fixed so the change can be interpreted.

lesson.title: Nuisance versus confound
lesson.body: A nuisance variable can add noise even when it is unrelated to the intervention. A confound changes with the intervention and offers a competing explanation for the result.

lesson.title: Levels of evidence
lesson.body: A smoke run proves that the pipeline and instrumentation work. A pilot estimates a plausible effect. A confirmatory run tests a frozen hypothesis and protocol at a sufficient budget.

lesson.title: Choosing a budget
lesson.body: Fixed steps compares update count; fixed tokens compares data exposure; fixed FLOPs compares approximate compute; fixed wall time compares practical value on the actual machine.

rubric.label: Experimental definitions
rubric.requirement: Correctly distinguishes intervention, outcome, controls, nuisance variables, and confounds.

rubric.label: Falsifiability
rubric.requirement: States a measurable, budgeted result that would reject the proposed mechanism.

rubric.label: Evidence levels
rubric.requirement: Separates smoke, pilot, and confirmatory evidence without overclaiming.

rubric.label: Comparison budget
rubric.requirement: Chooses among fixed steps, tokens, FLOPs, and wall time based on the claim.

activities.title: Audit a run and freeze the protocol
activities.summary: Use real run evidence to prove the laboratory loop is trustworthy.
activities.prompt: Attach the w0-smoke run and your protocol. Identify which artifact is immutable provenance, which files are derived convenience, what information would be lost by retaining only final validation BPB, and three invalid comparisons (measurement, control, and selection failures). End with a measurable divergence rule and test-set policy.

rubric.label: Artifact audit
rubric.requirement: Accurately uses manifest, log, metrics, summary, and workspace evidence.

rubric.label: Frozen protocol
rubric.requirement: Defines machine conditions, naming, interruption, divergence, and evaluation rules.

rubric.label: Invalid comparisons
rubric.requirement: Explains measurement, control, and selection failures with convincing mechanisms.

rubric.label: Reproducibility
rubric.requirement: Another researcher could recover the exact run and intended comparison.

activities.title: Reason from bytes to BPB
activities.summary: Prove that tokenizer comparisons and capacity accounting are valid.
activities.prompt: Explain how BPE starts and learns merges, derive bits-per-byte from total response NLL in nats and non-special bytes, and explain why cross-tokenizer perplexity is invalid. For the d6 model, identify every parameter category that changes with vocabulary and show how a larger vocabulary can reduce tokens per document while increasing capacity and compute. Include one concrete fair follow-up beyond a 600-step token-matched pilot.

rubric.label: BPE mechanism
rubric.requirement: Correctly explains starting symbols, merges, segmentation, and vocabulary tradeoffs.

rubric.label: BPB derivation
rubric.requirement: Derives the correct normalization and rejects incomparable tokenizer perplexities.

rubric.label: Capacity accounting
rubric.requirement: Identifies all vocabulary-dependent tensors and relevant compute consequences.

rubric.label: Fair comparison
rubric.requirement: Designs a byte- or FLOP-aware confirmation and calibrates the conclusion.

activities.title: Diagnose the pretraining baseline
activities.summary: Turn curves, throughput, and samples into a defensible model diagnosis.
activities.prompt: Attach your w1-baseline run and model card. Trace the key tensor shapes through one batch, reconcile the parameter/token calculation with the run, and diagnose warmup, plateau, warmdown, train-versus-validation movement, throughput drift, and sample evolution. Decide whether the evidence supports underfitting, overfitting, instability, or none of these, and name the cheapest falsifying follow-up.

rubric.label: Shapes & accounting
rubric.requirement: Correctly traces tensors and reconciles parameters, tokens, and approximate FLOPs.

rubric.label: Curve diagnosis
rubric.requirement: Uses the actual learning curves and schedule regions rather than final metrics alone.

rubric.label: Run evidence
rubric.requirement: Connects claims to immutable execution IDs, metrics, throughput, and examples.

rubric.label: Calibrated conclusion
rubric.requirement: Separates observation from inference and proposes a decisive follow-up.

activities.title: Untangle a joint intervention
activities.summary: Design comparisons that isolate mechanism rather than merely rank configurations.
activities.prompt: Choose one optimization family and one scaling/architecture family from Week 2. For each, state the causal question, mechanism, prediction, falsifier, independent variable, hidden joint interventions, and correct budget axes. You must address nanochat's automatic batch/LR coupling and explain why fixed-step depth, width, head, or context results are not automatically compute matched.

rubric.label: Causal question
rubric.requirement: Defines one-variable questions and mechanisms rather than winner searches.

rubric.label: Joint interventions
rubric.requirement: Finds batch/LR and architecture/compute couplings specific to nanochat.

rubric.label: Budget axes
rubric.requirement: Uses steps, tokens, FLOPs, parameters, and wall time according to the claim.

rubric.label: Confirmation plan
rubric.requirement: Freezes falsifiers, meaningful effects, and matched confirmatory runs.

activities.title: Prove an implementation contract
activities.summary: Demonstrate that a new architecture or optimization switch changes only what it claims.
activities.prompt: Attach the implementation and tests for one starred Week 2 contract. Explain the baseline-preserving default, checkpoint metadata, parameter/FLOP accounting, optimizer coverage, and the unit test written before training. Show the w0-smoke compatibility evidence. If the intervention changes capacity (for example SwiGLU or tied weights), distinguish raw from parameter-matched comparisons.

rubric.label: Implementation correctness
rubric.requirement: The switch implements the intended mechanism without accidental changes.

rubric.label: Independent tests
rubric.requirement: Tests cover invariants, gradients/optimizer ownership, and the new behavior.

rubric.label: Baseline compatibility
rubric.requirement: Defaults, checkpoints, metrics, and the smoke run remain compatible.

rubric.label: Fair accounting
rubric.requirement: Parameter and FLOP changes are measured and reflected in comparison claims.

activities.title: Defend an ablation portfolio
activities.summary: Convert many pilots into a small number of calibrated, confirmed conclusions.
activities.prompt: Attach your ablation portfolio and representative run IDs. Defend at least one positive, one null or negative, and one surprising result. For each: give the effect size, resource cost, confounds, strength label, and cheapest decisive follow-up. Explain why confirming only the pilot winner is biased and show how at least one claimed effect survives a larger-budget control/intervention pair.

rubric.label: Controlled coverage
rubric.requirement: Representative experiments use correct controls and resource accounting.

rubric.label: Confirmation discipline
rubric.requirement: Control and intervention are confirmed together under a frozen larger budget.

rubric.label: Negative evidence
rubric.requirement: Null, negative, and surprising results are retained and interpreted honestly.

rubric.label: Calibrated claims
rubric.requirement: Effect sizes, uncertainty, confounds, and follow-ups bound every conclusion.

activities.title: Trace the SFT learning signal
activities.summary: Explain exactly which tokens teach the model and which training state is inherited.
activities.prompt: Trace one conversation through serialization, packing, token IDs, shifted targets, response-only loss masking, and optimizer update. Identify prompts, padding, assistant outputs, and tool content that should or should not receive loss. Explain why loading optimizer state is an intervention and design a control for it. Finally, distinguish changing the data mixture at fixed examples, tokens, and steps.

rubric.label: Serialization & masking
rubric.requirement: Correctly identifies the supervised token positions and packing behavior.

rubric.label: Inherited training state
rubric.requirement: Explains optimizer/checkpoint inheritance and proposes a valid control.

rubric.label: Data-mixture reasoning
rubric.requirement: Separates fixed-example, fixed-token, and fixed-step interpretations.

rubric.label: Evaluation logic
rubric.requirement: Rejects impressionistic chat quality as sufficient evidence.

activities.title: Separate capability gain from forgetting
activities.summary: Use a frozen matrix and fixed prompts to measure what SFT added and removed.
activities.prompt: Attach the same-parent base, SFT baseline, and math-heavy SFT evidence plus your memo. Defend the frozen evaluation matrix, quantify instruction/format gains and base-capability regression separately, analyze the SFT curves, and classify representative failures from the fixed prompt suite. State which conclusion is robust and which remains confounded.

rubric.label: Controlled lineage
rubric.requirement: All compared SFT variants share the intended base parent and frozen suite.

rubric.label: Capability & forgetting
rubric.requirement: Measures both gains and regressions with relevant held-out metrics.

rubric.label: Fixed failure analysis
rubric.requirement: Uses categorized fixed prompts rather than selected anecdotes.

rubric.label: Bounded conclusion
rubric.requirement: Distinguishes formatting, instruction following, and knowledge acquisition.

activities.title: Derive DPO from response log ratios
activities.summary: Show what DPO optimizes before relying on an implementation.
activities.prompt: Derive the DPO loss for one chosen/rejected pair from response-token log probabilities under the policy and frozen reference. Explain prompt/padding masking, why response log probabilities are sums, why the reference is frozen, the limits as beta approaches zero or becomes large, and how response length can bias the comparison. Include a tiny numerical example with a hand-computed loss.

rubric.label: Loss derivation
rubric.requirement: Correctly derives the policy/reference chosen-rejected log-ratio loss.

rubric.label: Masking & length
rubric.requirement: Handles response tokens, padding, prompts, and length bias correctly.

rubric.label: Beta & reference
rubric.requirement: Explains the frozen reference and beta limits without treating beta as a generic LR.

rubric.label: Numerical hand check
rubric.requirement: Provides a reproducible calculation that can validate code independently.

activities.title: Verify DPO and audit preference drift
activities.summary: Prove the loss is right, then test whether preference accuracy is meaningful.
activities.prompt: Attach your DPO implementation, unit tests, data card, and study memo. Show the hand-calculated batch match, swap test, neutral-pair result, frozen-reference gradients, and masking test. Then defend the train/validation preference split and analyze beta, corrupted labels, rejected difficulty, capability retention, KL proxy, length, and at least one stylistic shortcut or ambiguity.

rubric.label: Independent verification
rubric.requirement: All required loss, masking, swap, neutral, and gradient tests are convincing.

rubric.label: Preference data audit
rubric.requirement: Split, corruption, ambiguity, and rejected difficulty are auditable.

rubric.label: Controlled beta/quality study
rubric.requirement: Measures held-out preference behavior under controlled interventions.

rubric.label: Drift & failures
rubric.requirement: Checks capability, KL proxy, length, style shortcuts, and qualitative failures.

activities.title: Trace the policy-gradient update
activities.summary: Explain nanochat's on-policy objective and why it is not full GRPO or PPO.
activities.prompt: Trace one GSM8K item from prompt through multiple rollouts, reward extraction, group-mean advantage, response-token log probabilities, accumulation, and update. Derive −A times the response log-probability sum. Explain why the group mean is a baseline, what happens when all rewards are equal, how length/normalization changes updates, and which GRPO/PPO components nanochat omits or modifies.

rubric.label: End-to-end trace
rubric.requirement: Accurately follows data, rollouts, rewards, masks, advantages, and updates.

rubric.label: Objective derivation
rubric.requirement: Correctly derives and interprets the implemented policy-gradient loss.

rubric.label: Group baseline & length
rubric.requirement: Explains zero-variance groups and normalization/length effects.

rubric.label: GRPO/PPO comparison
rubric.requirement: Precisely identifies missing reference KL, ratios/clipping, z-scores, and reuse.

activities.title: Interrogate reward improvement
activities.summary: Decide whether higher reward represents better reasoning or a measurement exploit.
activities.prompt: Attach same-parent group-size runs and your fixed-output audit. Jointly analyze reward, pass@1, pass@k, response length, wall time, and nonzero advantage variance. Explain the information/compute tradeoff for group sizes 2, 4, 8, and 16. Classify verifier failures and reward hacking, and state what can be concluded if reward rises while pass@1 is flat.

rubric.label: Joint metric analysis
rubric.requirement: Reward, pass@k, length, variance, and wall time are interpreted together.

rubric.label: Group-size control
rubric.requirement: Separates rollout information, variance, compute, and fixed-time update count.

rubric.label: Reward-hacking audit
rubric.requirement: Uses a frozen, categorized output audit to test verifier validity.

rubric.label: Calibrated conclusion
rubric.requirement: Does not equate reward or pass@k movement with reasoning improvement.

activities.title: Freeze the Parameter Golf competition
activities.summary: Make the 30-minute objective fair before observing the search results.
activities.prompt: Attach the committed capstone protocol and reproducible entrypoint. Define the timer, hardware, data/tokenizer, validation split, sealed test, checkpoint limit, precomputation, and retry rules. Show the official d6, best-single-intervention, and simple-alternative baselines. Explain the staged search, interaction tests, candidate lock, exact reproduction, and one-time final test.

rubric.label: Frozen fair rules
rubric.requirement: Every budget, data, evaluation, artifact, and failure rule is operational and precommitted.

rubric.label: Required baselines
rubric.requirement: The official, strongest single, and simple baselines answer distinct questions.

rubric.label: Evidence-driven search
rubric.requirement: Pilots, confirmations, interactions, lock, reproduction, and final test are staged correctly.

rubric.label: Exact entrypoint
rubric.requirement: One command verifies provenance, isolates artifacts, runs, logs, and evaluates.

activities.title: Defend the final model—and the discarded ideas
activities.summary: Earn mastery by explaining causal evidence, uncertainty, reproduction, and limits.
activities.prompt: Attach the final report and run evidence. State one measured claim with budget and effect size. Defend the ablation ladder, validation-versus-time and tokens, throughput tails, reproduction difference, and test gap. Identify the strongest causal intervention, the result most likely to be selection noise, a change that helps per token but hurts per minute, five discarded ideas, and the conclusion least likely to scale beyond d6.

rubric.label: Measured result
rubric.requirement: The final claim includes metric, effect size, budget, baseline, and reproduction.

rubric.label: Causal evidence
rubric.requirement: The ablation ladder and interactions justify the selected configuration.

rubric.label: Test & negative-result discipline
rubric.requirement: The sealed test, discarded ideas, uncertainty, and selection risks are reported honestly.

rubric.label: Scientific communication
rubric.requirement: Claims are concise, reproducible, calibrated, and bounded beyond the local setting.
